Synopsis:
GBP is on its fourth consecutive weekly gain, trading near ~$1.3658, supported by a weak dollar and sticky UK inflation keeping BoE rate-hike expectations alive through 2026-2027. A divergence exists between economist consensus (rates on hold) and market pricing (at least one hike in 2026). Dollar weakness is attributed to concerns that US Treasury bond-market interventions may be undermining USD confidence. UK retail sales dipped in July after a June surge; government recorded an unexpected budget deficit.
